question.text: A wire loop <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi><mi>Q</mi><mi>R</mi></math> having the shape of a right-angle triangle with <math> <mrow> <mi>P</mi><mi>Q</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow> </math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> carries a steady current <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>I</mi></math>. If the magnitude of the magnetic field at the point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi><mo> </mo></math>due to this loop is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>k</mi><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mi>I</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>48</mn><mi>π</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></math>, then find the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>k</mi></math>.

solution.text:
The magnetic field at P due to current elements PQ and PR

is zero as the point P is on the conductor. Therefore, the magnetic field at P due to current element QR is

B=μ0I4π(PD)sinϕ1+sinϕ2

=μ01×54π×12x9x53x+16x54x

=μ0I×548πx35+45

=748μ0Iπx
